queries.question: What does the accepted bounded candidate-buffer model take, execute, and prove against authentic Tunnels of Doom?
queries.answer: The neutral model starts at GPL >8246 with a kernel-entry seed, the 538-byte >34B8..>36D1 payload, one-cell VRAM context, and the proven count/position/control bytes. It performs the decoded reset, 23 accepted seed-dependent stores, alternating stride->0020 and stride->0001 propagation passes twice, and adjacent-cell cleanup using the authentic RAND LCG. It exactly reproduces the accepted >5207 and >82F0 kernel-entry cases. A prediction for the predeclared unseen seed >A5C3 was frozen first; one authentic run then matched all 538 bytes (SHA-256 58f44c03d67b41d19cd966d632ac1020da86f6e7c2430fdf5014d4c97b73e913), next seed >AF57, completion through >84F1, 1,178 writes, 92 RAND calls, and 31 placement attempts. Byte meanings, later content/stocking, inter-floor contracts, and general >857B retry behavior remain unresolved.
